items.body_md:
On August 10, the docket in *In re Oriel Bachar and Papaya Gaming Ltd.*, No. 26-11217 (Bankr. D. Del.), recorded no new filings, with activity frozen at the three Skillz deposition notices (Dkts. 53–55) and the accompanying notice of service (Dkt. 52) entered August 8 — all covered in the prior edition.

The substantive posture is unchanged. 
Judge Walrath rejected Skillz's demands and granted Papaya's request for a temporary injunction
, as reported by __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__ — that grant, entered before this window opened, remains the operative protection. 
Papaya filed for Chapter 15 recognition in Delaware to prevent Skillz from taking unilateral action to seize U.S. assets while the appeal is pending, and Judge Walrath's temporary injunction now provides Papaya with legal protection while the Chapter 15 proceedings move forward.
 The financial gap driving this proceeding has not narrowed: 
Judge Cote ordered Papaya to pay approximately $719 million in disgorgement, as well as approximately $10.1 million in attorneys' fees and legal costs,
 per __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__, against a Tel Aviv-supervised fund 
into which Papaya will place available cash overseen by a court-appointed official, expected to contain around $100 million during 2026 along with additional annual contributions,
 per __[World Casino Directory](https://news.worldcasinodirectory.com/papaya-gaming-files-chapter-15-after-719m-verdict-123873)__.

The next hard milestones remain the objection deadline of August 27, 2026, and the recognition hearing before Judge Walrath on September 3, 2026, at 9:30 AM (virtual). Skillz's decision to notice depositions of Bachar, Yaniv, and Kong before that hearing — already noted — signals a factual contest over the center-of-main-interests determination rather than a purely legal objection; whether those depositions have been scheduled and confirmed will be the first indicator of whether Skillz is pressing that challenge at full speed or using the notices as leverage ahead of any negotiated resolution.

items.body_md:
On August 9, Thor CALAP LLC's no-cause diligence termination right under both West Texas purchase agreements expired by its own contractual terms. 
Thor had the right to terminate either deal over unsatisfactory diligence through August 9, five days before the court's scheduled bidding-procedures hearing.
 No termination notice has appeared on the docket as of this writing, and no press outlet has reported exercise of that right. That absence is consistent with both agreements remaining operative, but it is not confirmatory: a termination notice delivered directly to the debtors would not necessarily surface as an immediate court filing. The status of the $52 million floor — and by extension the stalking-horse protections that anchor the September auction calendar — remains unverified until the debtors affirmatively represent the agreements are in effect, a termination notice hits the docket, or the August 14 hearing proceeds on the assumption the stalking horse is intact.

The August 14 hearing before Judge O'Hagan at 11 a.m. ET now carries the full weight of the downstream calendar. At least one live objection to the bidding-procedures and sale motion was filed on the August 7 deadline at Dkt. 98, with an accompanying document at Dkt. 99 and exhibit at Dkt. 100 filed August 8; the identity of the objecting party and the specific grounds remain unestablished from available docket text. How Judge O'Hagan resolves that objection — and whether he approves the bidding procedures on the debtors' proposed timeline — determines whether the September 8 qualified-bid deadline and September 10 auction date hold. 
The Assigned Contracts Schedule, with proposed cure amounts, is due August 21, 2026
 — a week after the hearing — meaning the question of which power supply, scheduling, and interconnection agreements transfer with the Pyote and Tarbush assets will not be resolved before Judge O'Hagan rules on the sale framework. 
The Assumed Contracts and Excluded Assets schedules are blank in both APAs, and Thor may remove any assumed contract before closing; because the debtors contract through FlowX rather than directly with TNMP, the record does not establish which supply, scheduling, or interconnection agreements would transfer with the assets.


For the 11,700 wallet holders carrying $163,723,500 in unsecured IOU claims, Thursday's hearing is the first concrete read on whether the estate's sale process is intact. 
Both purchase agreements leave the allocation of consideration between the two Lonestar estates to the buyer, to be determined within 180 days after closing, and Poolin Technology is not a seller under either agreement
 — a structural gap that compounds the uncertainty already embedded in estate-level lien analysis, transfer taxes, professional fees, and the treatment of Poolin's intercompany claim. The next concrete milestone is the August 14 hearing at 11 a.m. ET; what moves there sets or collapses the entire September auction calendar.

items.lede: On August 7, an unidentified party filed a motion for relief from the automatic stay at Dkt. 146 in Case No. 26-90737, supported by affidavits at Dkts. 156 and 157 filed the same day and served through the BNC certificate of mailing at Dkt. 158 on August 8.
items.body_md:
On August 7, an unidentified party filed a motion for relief from the automatic stay at Dkt. 146 in Case No. 26-90737, supported by affidavits at Dkts. 156 and 157 filed the same day and served through the BNC certificate of mailing at Dkt. 158 on August 8. The movant's identity, the specific asset or claim at issue, and the precise relief sought remain unverified without a PACER pull of the document itself; that caveat carries forward from the prior briefing and is not resolved by anything that landed over the weekend. What is confirmed from the docket is that service is complete and the contested-matter timeline is running.

Under Bankruptcy Local Rule 4001 in the Southern District of Texas, a response to a lift-stay motion is ordinarily due 14 days after service. With the BNC certificate issued August 8, the response deadline falls approximately August 22 — two days before the August 24 second-day hearing. That timing makes Dkt. 146 a live candidate for the August 24 docket, either as a fully contested matter if a response is filed, or by agreed resolution between filing and the hearing date. Either path is material to recovery posture: if the movant seeks to reach estate property — inventory, a receivable, a leased facility — any grant of stay relief before the estate has conducted a sale process removes that asset from the pool available to unsecured creditors. If the motion targets something outside the estate (third-party collateral, a non-debtor guarantor), the impact is more contained. Confirmation of the document's contents remains the threshold step before the consequence can be sized.

The remainder of the 72-hour window — Dkts. 147 through 155, and Dkt. 158 — consists entirely of pro hac vice admissions, notices of appearance, and the BNC certificate: procedural and routine, omitted per the materiality filter. No new press coverage has landed since the Drinks Business piece of August 3. The next concrete milestone is the second-day hearing before Judge Lopez on August 24, 2026, at which the lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146 and the first-day-to-final conversions are the two open substantive items, alongside the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors' first formal appearance on the record.
